newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: France open to p'ships on Thomson-CSF sale.
newsitem.headline: France open to p'ships on Thomson-CSF sale.

text.p: France is open to partnerships among companies bidding to buy defence electronics group Thomson-CSF, French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Saturday.

He had been asked if the government was actively encouraging Britain's GEC to line up with French companies bidding for Thomson-CSF. GEC's own bid was rejected on Friday as against national security interests.
"The government is open to partnerships," he told a news conference after a meeting of European Union finance ministers in this Dutch seaside town.
"The government is ready to examine offers which include partnerships," he added.
France on Friday declared as acceptable intentions to bid submitted by electronics-to-publishing group Lagardere and electronics and engineering company Alcatel Alsthom .

"However, because the sale to a foreign company of more than 50 percent of the share capital of Thomson-CSF goes against the interests of national security, the proposal by GEC has not been admitted," it added.
The French state controls 58 percent of Thomson-CSF.

Arthuis also suggested that bringing a non-French partner into a bid for Thomson-CSF would counter the risk that by rejecting GEC, France would fail in its ambition of creating a big European defence company capable of competing with U.S. giants.
"The principle of a partnership avoids that risk," he said.
GEC said on Friday that it would hold talks with the two French companies bidding for Thomson-CSF and that the French government had encouraged it to do so.

Analysts had seen its declaration of interest in buying Thomson-CSF as a means of winning a stake in the company, since they said it had always seemed clear France would never allow a defence company to fall into foreign, albeit European, hands.

France had to cancel a previous attempt last year to privatise Thomson-CSF parent Thomson SA after the independent Privatisation Commission objected to the sale of Thomson subsidiary Thomson Multimedia to South Korea's Daewoo Electronics.
The government had already expressed a preference for a bid by Lagardere, which planned to buy all of the Thomson group but sell on Thomson Multimedia to the South Korean company.
Thomson-CSF is now being sold on its own.
